 title: 'Manage work: customer service: help with self calculation after 31 October'
 ---
 
-## Background
+**Background**
 
-It is our policy to give help to customers to enable them to complete their self calculations. But, we need to ensure that the benefits of filing a paper return by 31 October after the end of the return year are both real and visible to the public. A paper return filed after 31 October will have been received after the filing date, and the customer will be liable to an automatic late filing penalty.
+It is our policy to give help to customers to enable them to complete their self-calculations. But we need to ensure that the benefits of filing a paper return by 31 October after the end of the return year, are both real and visible to the public. A paper return filed after 31 October will have been received after the filing date and the customer will be liable to an automatic late filing penalty.
 
-## Customer options
+**Customer options – Late paper Self-Assessment Filing**
 
-After 31 October, customers have four options. They can
+After 31 October, customers have four options when filing a paper Self-Assessment Return. They can:
 
-|  |  |
-| --- | --- |
-| 1. | Complete and file their tax return online. All of the Software and Online forms will calculate their tax liability for them. They will have until 31 January to file online, without incurring an automatic late filing penalty |
-|  |  |
-| 2. | Attempt the self calculation and come back for help if they are having difficulty with particular points. The paper return should have been filed by 31 October so they will be liable to an automatic late filing penalty |
-| 3. | Complete the self calculation without our help. We will correct it if it is wrong, but cannot guarantee to do so in time to tell him / her how much to pay by 31 January. The paper return should have been filed by 31 October so they will be liable to an automatic late filing penalty |
-| 4. | Submit the return without doing the self calculation. If so, we will still calculate the tax due, but cannot guarantee to do so in time to tell him / her how much to pay by 31 January. The paper return should have been filed by 31 October so they will be liable to an automatic late filing penalty |
+* Complete and file their tax return online. All of the software and online forms will calculate their tax liability for them. They will have until 31 January to file online, without incurring an automatic late filing penalty
+* Attempt the self calculation and come back for help if they are having difficulty with particular points. The paper return should have been filed by 31 October, so they will be liable to an automatic late filing penalty
+* Complete the self calculation without our help. We will correct it if it is wrong, but cannot guarantee to do so in time to tell them, how much to pay by 31 January. The paper return should have been filed by 31 October, so they will be liable to an automatic late filing penalty
+* Submit the return without doing the self calculation. If so, we will still calculate the tax due, but cannot guarantee to do so in time to tell them, how much to pay by 31 January. The paper return should have been filed by 31 October, so they will be liable to an automatic late filing penalty
 
-With options 3 and 4 the customer has to accept the risk of interest and surcharge, for tax years 2009-2010 and earlier, or late payment penalties for 2010-2011 and later, arising if we cannot tell him / her how much to pay by 31 January. The customer will be liable to an automatic late filing penalty in either case.
+Guidance regarding penalties for the tax years 2010-11 and later, can be found under [SAM61200](https://www.gov.uk/hmrc-internal-manuals/self-assessment-manual/sam61200) onwards.
 
-## Penalty capping
+**Customers seeking help**
 
-For the tax years 2009-10, and earlier, the amount of the penalty was linked to the amount of the SA debt outstanding at close of business on 31 January.
+Your approach to customers seeking help after 31 October, depends on the extent to which the customers have attempted to self-calculate.
 
-If a customer had paid all of the tax due, the penalty was capped at £0.00.
+If the customer is having difficulty with particular points on the self-calculation, you should provide assistance. The customer must have attempted to complete their SA return in full and be able to give the details from their completed return over the telephone.
 
-Similarly, if an SA underpayment of less than £2,000 had been transferred to PAYE to be collected through a PAYE code during the following tax year, then the amount of the SA debt (tax due on 31 January) was nil, again the penalty would be capped at £0.00.
+SA Tax Calculators are available on the SEES menu in excel and can be used to assist customers with their self-calculation on the telephone.
 
-Guidance regarding penalties for the tax years 2010-11 and later, can be found under [SAM61200](https://www.gov.uk/hmrc-internal-manuals/self-assessment-manual/sam61200) onwards.
+* If the customer has made little or no attempt to complete the self-calculation and asks to be guided through the whole form, or substantial parts of it, you should refuse the request, unless the taxpayer is incapable of completing the self-calculation - (see ‘Extra Assistance' below)
 
-## Customers seeking help
+* Advise that the 31 October was the deadline for paper returns to have been filed, and for customers who wanted HMRC to work out their tax for them in time, to be told how much to pay by 31 January
 
-Your approach to customers seeking help after 31 October depends on the extent to which the customers have attempted to self calculate.
+* Advise that if the paper return is filed late, an automatic late filing penalty may be charged
 
-If the customer is having difficulty with particular points on the self calculation, you should give help, to the same extent as you would for other parts of the return, on the aspects which are troubling him / her.
+* Advise of the benefits of online filing
 
-SA Tax Calculators are available on the SEES menu in Excel and can be used to
+**Extra Assistance**
 
-* Check a self calculating customer’s liability on the telephone
+If a customer is incapable of completing the self-calculation and asks you to complete it for them, you should do so. This will usually only arise, where similar help has been needed with completion of the return.
 
-Or
-
-* Assist customers with their self calculation on the telephone
-
-However before assistance is given, the customer must have completed their SA return in full and be able to give the details from their completed return over the telephone.
-
-If the customer has made little or no attempt to complete the self calculation and asks to be guided through the whole form or substantial parts of it you should
-
-* Refuse the request politely but firmly, unless the taxpayer is incapable of completing the self calculation (see ‘Special needs’ below)
-* Advise that the 31 October was the well-publicised deadline for paper returns to have been filed, and for customers who wanted HMRC to work their tax for them in time to be told how much to pay by 31 January
-* Advise that if the paper return is filed late, an automatic late filing penalty may be charged
-* Advise of the benefits of online filing
-* Explain the four customer options open to the taxpayer
-

-
-If a customer is effectively incapable of completing the self calculation, and asks you to complete it for him / her, you should do so. This will usually arise only where similar help has been needed with completion of the return.
-

+Customers that require extra assistance, include those who:

+You will need to use your discretion to decide whether individual customers are unable to complete forms themselves, but it is not necessary to ask for proof. If you are in doubt, seek your manager’s, or a colleague’s advice.

+* [SAM70150 – Visually Impaired Media Unit](https://www.gov.uk/hmrc-internal-manuals/self-assessment-manual/sam70150)

-Those customers who prefer to leave the calculation to HMRC may ask for advice on what first payment on account to make by 31 January. If so, advise
+We will calculate their bill in due course. But because their return was received after the deadline for paper returns and for Revenue Calculation on 31 October, we may not be able to do so, until after 31 January.

+Those customers who prefer to leave the calculation to HMRC, may ask for advice on what first payment on account to make by 31 January. If so, you can advise as per the below:

+* Self-employed customers to make a payment based on whatever they paid last year, adjusted to the extent that they estimate their profits have increased or decreased
+
+* PAYE customers to pay 20 per cent of any untaxed income
+
+In either case, stress this is only a rough estimate and will not necessarily be correct and that in future, the best way to be sure of the correct figure is by either:
+

+
+* Complete and file their tax return online - this is the preferred option. All of the software and online forms, will calculate their tax liability for them. They will have until 31 January to file online, without incurring an automatic late filing penalty

+| **SRS Role**  **ETMP** | **Description** |
+| Create / Cancel Repayments | HMRC users require a specific role to be assigned, in order to perform actions via the UI5 screen, to create and cancel MTD ITSA repayment requests. |
+| Enter Repayment Bank Details | Allows an HMRC adviser to input new repayment bank details, for customers or agents.  Allows an HMRC adviser to amend or override existing bank details, for customers or agents.  Allows an HMRC adviser to input customer's bank details, to create a repayment. |
+| ETMP ITSA PR Manually Raise a Charge | This allows the user to raise and amend manual late payment penalty charges and to create and amend Contract Notes via ETMP for ITSA customers. |
+| High Value Repayment Approver | Approves high‑value repayments above a set limit Scheme of Delegated Authority (SoDA). |
+| Initiate / Cancel Coding Out | Gives advisors the ability to create and cancel coding‑out requests for ITSA underpayments, via the UI5 application in ETMP. It is specific to coding-out only and does not allow creation or amendment of tax returns. |
+| ITSA Claim to Reduce | The ITSA amend role, displays the ITSA taxpayer overview for the ITSA customer.  The HMRC user requires this role to be assigned, in order to access and edit certain fields of the form bundle only. They can view information such as master data, returns, as well as the functionality to process amendments to the value of the ITSA POA1 and POA2 items on taxpayers’ accounts, using the UI5 gateway service. |
+| ITSA Manager | Manages the ITSA work queue and allocates work to staff.  **Cannot** be allocated with **ETMP ITSA Tax Officer**. |
+| ITSA Ringfenced Category - Economic Crime - Access Role | Business individual category taxpayers, allowing HMRC tax officers to carry out all ITSA-related business processes, for taxpayers within this category.  This role must be paired with the 'RW1406 ITSA Ringfenced Category – Maintenance Role'. |
+| ITSA Ringfenced Category - Expats - Access Role | The "ITSA Ringfenced Category – Expats – Access" role provides full access to ITSA Ringfenced Expats category taxpayers, allowing HMRC tax officers to carry out all ITSA-related business processes for taxpayers within this category.  This role must be paired with the 'RW1406 ITSA Ringfenced Category – Maintenance Role.' |
+| ITSA Ringfenced Category - Foreign Entertainers Unit - Access Role | The "ITSA Ringfenced Category – FEU (Foreign Entertainers Unit) – Access" role, provides full access to ITSA Ringfenced FEU (Foreign Entertainers Unit) category taxpayers, allowing HMRC tax officers to carry out all ITSA-related business processes, for taxpayers within this category.  This role must be paired with the 'RW1406 ITSA Ringfenced Category – Maintenance Role.' |
+| ITSA Ringfenced Category - Large Business Individual - Access Role | The "ITSA Ringfenced Category – Large Business Individual – Access" role, provides full access to ITSA Ringfenced Large Business Individual category taxpayers, allowing HMRC tax officers to carry out all ITSA-related business processes, for taxpayers within this category.  This role must be paired with the 'RW1406 ITSA Ringfenced Category – Maintenance Role’. |
+| ITSA Ringfenced Category - Remittance Basis Charge - Access Role | The "ITSA Ringfenced Category – RBC (Remittance Basis Charge) – Access" role, provides full access to ITSA Ringfenced RBC (Remittance Basis Charge) category taxpayers, allowing HMRC tax officers to carry out all ITSA-related business processes, for taxpayers within this category.  This role must be paired with the 'RW1406 ITSA Ringfenced Category – Maintenance Role.' |
+| ITSA Ringfenced Category – SARP SA Record Protection - Access Role | The "ITSA Ringfenced Category – SARP (SA Record Protection) Access" role, provides full access to ITSA Ringfenced SARP category taxpayers, allowing HMRC tax officers to carry out all ITSA-related business processes, for taxpayers within this category.  This role must be paired with the 'RW1406 ITSA Ringfenced Category – Maintenance Role.' |
+| ITSARingfenced Category - Wealthy 1 - Access Role | The "ITSA Ringfenced Category – Wealthy 1 – Access" role, provides full access to ITSA Ringfenced Wealthy 1 category taxpayers, allowing HMRC tax officers to carry out all ITSA-related business processes, for taxpayers within this category.  This role must be paired with the 'RW1406 ITSA Ringfenced Category – Maintenance Role.' |
+| ITSARingfenced Category - Wealthy 2 - Access Role | The "ITSA Ringfenced Category – Wealthy 2 – Access" role, provides full access to ITSA Ringfenced Wealthy 2 category taxpayers, allowing HMRC tax officers to carry out all ITSA-related business processes, for taxpayers within this category.  This role must be paired with the 'RW1406 ITSA Ringfenced Category – Maintenance Role.' |
+| ITSA Super User | Sets up teams and assigns users to roles and structures. |
+| ITSA Tax Officer | Allows the advisor to access the customer’s record and complete day‑to‑day actions on ETMP records.  **Cannot** be allocated with:  **RW1403**: ETMP ITSA Manager  **PC0032**: SAFE Repayment Approver  **PC0154**: ITSA Create / Cancel Manual Financial Adjustments |
+| ITSA PR Penalty Processor | Allows advisors to manage penalty points and late payment / late submission penalties, using a dedicated SAP UI5 application. |
+| ITSA PR Penalty View Only | View‑only access for penalty information. |

+| Manual Financial Adjustments | Allows the adviser to manually add or cancel debit or credit adjustments.  **Cannot** be allocated with **ETMP ITSA Tax Officer**. |
+| MTDB HIB Amend Opt Out | Enables an MTD user to opt out of 'quarterly submissions'. |

+| MTDB HiB Wealthy 1 Access | Enables the HMRC user to view 'Wealthy 1' customer records in HiB. |
+| MTDB HiB Wealthy 2 Access | Enables the HMRC user to view 'Wealthy2' customer records in HiB. |
+| No Repayment Signal (NRS) | HMRC user's require this role to be assigned.   To maintain and have an option to edit the No Repayment Signal information. |
+| Repayment Inhibit Worklist | The role will provide the user with access to a list of repayment work items, that an HMRC adviser will need to review.   These are cases where repayments are blocked or need further review. |
+| RT1402 ITSA Returns Amend | Advisers will need this to amend MTD returns (quarterly or finalised returns).  Required with MTDB HIB Amend. |
+| Safe Repayment Approver | Provides a HMRC user, authorisation to accept or reject a BACS, Payable Order or card repayment, that has been initiated by someone else.  **Cannot** be allocated with **ETMP ITSA Tax Officer**, or **ETMP ITSA Claim to Reduce** |
+| SAFE Payment Allocations | This role provides authorisation to a HMRC adviser to search, view and maintain documents and transactions for customer accounts. |

title: Making Tax Digital for income tax Self-Assessment: internal ETMP roles: guidance for managers
patch:
--- SAM230100@before
+++ SAM230100@after
@@ -0,0 +1,58 @@
+---
+base_path: /hmrc-internal-manuals/self-assessment-manual/sam230100
+public_updated_at: '2026-08-25T01:00:00+01:00'
+section_id: SAM230100
+title: 'Making Tax Digital for income tax Self-Assessment: internal ETMP roles: guidance
+  for managers'
+---
+
+As part of MTD, ITSA ETMP roles are available in SRS for you
+to assign to your team.
+
+When allocating roles, keep it simple — only give
+the combination of ITSA ETMP roles, the user needs to carry out their
+day-to-day job.
+
+There are some ITSA ETMP role combinations that should not
+be assigned together.
+
+These restrictions are in place to reduce risk, support a
+good customer service and help to reduce fraud.
+
+### What you need to check before assigning roles
+
+Not everyone will need the same level of ETMP access. Some
+staff will need more roles than others and users can have a combination of:
+
+• View access (read-only)
+
+• Edit access (to make changes)
+
+Before you submit a request, SRS
+will indicate whether a business case is required to
+support the allocation of these IT roles.
+
+You need to consider:
+
+• What does this person need to do in their role day-to-day?
+
+• What access they need and why?
+
+To avoid delays, try to include all required ITSA ETMP roles
+for each user, in a single SRS request.
+
+Where appropriate, bulk uploads will be done by CDIO.
+
+### Roles and access
+
+PT Operations - Line managers make requests via the Admin Team.
+
+Other directorates
+make requests via SRS and the instructions are below:
+
+* Go to Browse SRS
+* Go to User Management
+* Add services for a single user
+* Search by PID / name
+* Request roles as per
+  your Head of Duty
